title: A signal to make red cells
hook: Connect a hormonal signal with a target.

knows: Hormones can carry signals through the blood to target tissues.
doesNotKnow: Erythropoietin produced largely by the kidneys stimulates red blood cell production in the bone marrow, including in response to low oxygen availability.

misconception: All hormones come from one gland and act on every cell.
objective: Identify the stated endocrine signal and its target in a simplified pathway.

claims.text: Question, diagram and explanation: Which hormone produced mainly by the kidneys stimulates red blood cell production in bone marrow? Erythropoietin produced largely by the kidneys stimulates red blood cell production in the bone marrow, including in response to low oxygen availability.
The diagram shows one selected source–target pathway, not all hormone effects or feedback loops.

Recall: In the stated example, which source releases EPO into the circulation? Erythropoietin produced largely by the kidneys stimulates red blood cell production in the bone marrow, including in response to low oxygen availability.
